purpose: One machine-readable definition of the canonical NEMO source tree: what counts as source, what is generated, and exactly how the tree is enumerated and hashed. The transfer manifest binds this file by SHA-256 so the rules cannot drift silently.

canonical_source.definition: Authoritative source material only: regular files and symlinks the project maintains by hand. A clean checkout has exactly one canonical source identity.
examples: checked-in symlinks such as crates/*/LICENSE, CLAUDE.md, integrations/pi/*
canonical_source.rule: Running a build must not change this identity. Generated output never enters it.

generated_build.definition: Files derived deterministically from canonical source during a build or package step. They are reproducible; they are not source.
generated_build.rule: Enumerated out of canonical identity on BOTH trees. Presence or absence on disk must not change the digest or the transfer delta.

release_artifact.definition: The packaged distribution produced from canonical source plus deterministic generation/build steps. The exact bytes tested are the exact bytes signed and published.
release_artifact.rule: Qualified, hashed, and signed as immutable artifacts — never rebuilt between test and publish.

canonical_stream.exec_field: 'x' when any owner/group/other execute bit is set, '-' otherwise. The bit is security-relevant for shipped scripts (install.sh, scripts/qualification/*, packaging entry points); it is recorded explicitly rather than left implicit.
canonical_stream.path_encoding: Slash-separated, './'-prefixed, relative to the tree root. Raw filesystem bytes are preserved verbatim (os strings); no Unicode normalization is applied.
canonical_stream.ordering: Records are emitted in byte-wise lexicographic order of the normalized path (LC_ALL=C ordering). One normalized path produces exactly one record; a duplicate is rejected as a malformed enumeration.
canonical_stream.line_ending: Each record is terminated by a single LF (\n). No CRLF normalization exists anywhere: file CONTENT is hashed byte-verbatim, so line endings inside files are bound by the content digest.
canonical_stream.timestamps: Never hashed. mtime, atime, ctime, and archive metadata are not part of identity.
canonical_stream.other_objects: Anything that is neither a regular file nor a symlink (fifo, socket, device) is a malformed-tree condition, not a silent skip.

enumeration.generated_path_semantics: Tree-relative slash patterns. A trailing '/' names a directory subtree. '*' does not cross '/', '**' does. Entries are excluded from canonical enumeration on BOTH trees identically, so a generated file can never appear as an addition, removal, or modification in the transfer delta.
enumeration.forbidden_transient: Any filesystem object inside the canonical tree that is not excluded above and not declared by the transfer manifest is a verification failure — provenance fails loudly rather than silently absorbing local state. Notably, '.claude/' is deliberately NOT excluded: it is tracked in the frozen reference (.claude/skills symlink) and its removal from the canonical tree is a declared delta entry.

delta.rule: The declared delta must equal the computed delta between the frozen reference and the canonical tree exactly — every class, exhaustively.

verification_modes.shipping_tree: Does this runtime match its own declared canonical digest? May run without the frozen source (informational).
verification_modes.transfer_qualification: Can this runtime be proven to be the exact declared transformation from the frozen reference? REQUIRES the frozen source on disk; absence is a hard failure. Official release admission runs this mode.
